account: Today I inspected the mill and saw 74 hay bales. The baker later reported eighty loaves at one emerald each and wanted to learn whether households face access or affordability problems, so baking can match demand. I know of no specific households in difficulty. Several townspeople have repeated reports of a bridge or port change discussed at the bakery, supposedly involving the baker, builder, freight operator and innkeeper. I have not witnessed that discussion or any obstruction. The baker could not reliably recall a proposal or agreement, said the bridge was passable this morning, and reported that the innkeeper knew of no verified obstruction. Asking the builder or freight operator may clarify matters; the rumor's purpose and any actual proposed change remain unknown. Town administration is also short of information: no council letters arrived for my afternoon session, and the custodian of the financial ledger remains unidentified. I am now at the dockside cottage with the neighbour for my scheduled tea, somewhat after fifteen. I am due back at the office at sixteen-thirty. At eighteen I have a confirmed great-hall appointment concerning the innkeeper's community hospitality matter, attending alone with no preparation requested; the secretary is to remind and escort me. I do not yet know the details of that matter or whether it relates to the crossing reports.
